LHX.sentence: L3Harris has sold off hard and sits well below its high, but that's because the usual defense-spending tailwind just isn't pushing right now — the business itself hasn't changed.

ASML.sentence: ASML is quiet and barely moved, though after a big run it's gotten expensive — still, they remain the only company on earth that makes the machines used to print the most advanced chips, so demand isn't the worry.

LIN.sentence: Linde is drifting along as usual — selling oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen on long contracts and nudging prices up a little at a time, which is the whole steady story with this one.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — the Azure cloud and AI business keeps grinding along, though the stock is priced richly enough that there's not much room for disappointment.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher dipped a bit, but biotech funding is thawing out again, and since labs start spending on their equipment a couple of quarters later, that's an encouraging early sign for this picks-and-shovels supplier.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge slipped a bit, but this pipeline operator works like a toll road on oil and gas moving across North America, and its dividend remains fairly — though not spectacularly — attractive.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow bounced this week and is still well off its high, which is unusual for a company whose AI-automation tools keep winning big corporate and government contracts — a rare dip in a strong business.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore edged up and is paying a very generous dividend, with its big commodity-trading arm throwing off enough cash to keep those payouts well supported.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta was flat, and the headline price-per-ton looks like it fell only because of what they happened to sell — strip that out and the price of their rock is still climbing nicely, which is the whole point of this business.

KOF.sentence: This Latin American Coca-Cola bottler rose today, but that move is mostly the Mexican peso shifting against the dollar rather than anything new in how many bottles they're selling.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras dipped slightly, but with oil prices far above what it costs them to pump, the cash is pouring in and comfortably covering that very large dividend.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant that moves goods around the world by sea, rose a touch and is trading below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace — a classic sign of a bargain in a boom-and-bust industry.

MA.sentence: Mastercard was basically flat, and interestingly it's trading at the same price level as rival Visa even though it's the faster grower — unusual, since it normally commands a premium.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot company rose today and is unusually cheap compared with its own recent history, even as hospitals keep scheduling more and more robot-assisted operations — and every surgery means more supplies sold.
